text:
maya: quick check — noticed a user removal in Okta but downstream app access stayed for ~6 hours. SCIM logs show a `deprovision` event from Okta at 1769989900 but our app logs show continued activity. Could nested group membership be preventing immediate removal? also: are we allowed to log full corp emails in the auth pipeline logs? wondering if we should redact by default in ingestion.
samir: nested groups can be tricky — our SCIM mapping uses `groupFilter` and `members` sync, but if the app treats nested groups as first-class, removal from parent might not propagate unless nested membership was expanded at last sync. do we have an expand-nested setting turned on? :thinking:
jonathan: FYI Okta lifecycle_events can be delivered asynchronously; sometimes events are queued if their SCIM connector is throttled. that could explain the 6h gap. however, if the app caches group membership (we do prefix/KV cache for auth checks) and the cache ttl is long (default 4h), it might persist access. please check cache TTL in app-config.
maya: right — I checked app-config: `auth.group_cache_ttl = 4h`. combined with delivery lag could explain. on the logging side, our ELK ingestion currently stores `user.email` plaintext in the `auth_attempt` index. that's probably not ideal for PII. what do we want as the team default? hashed email? domain-only?
infra-bot: ingest pipeline snippet (logs):
```
{ "ts": 1769989905, "user": "mia.thompson@redwood.com", "action": "token_use", "resource": "internal-dashboard" }
{ "ts": 1769993001, "user": "mia.thompson@redwood.com", "action": "deprovision_received", "source": "okta_scim" }
```
maya: thanks — I'd prefer `user.email_hashed` and `user.email_domain` only. we should stop writing plaintext.

idp-bot: policy reminder — company retention/pseudonymization: "PII in logs must be pseudonymized within 24h unless explicit approval from Legal". See https://wiki/redwood/infosec/logging-policy :lock:
sophia: quick ops question — if we implement hashing at the log producer side, we'll still need the raw mapping for audits. propose: store raw email only in a short-lived secure audit index with stricter ACLs and then delete after 30d. everything else gets hashed + domain. :thumbsup:
jonathan: sounds good. for the SCIM/nested group fix: options = (1) reduce `auth.group_cache_ttl` to 5m for sensitive routes, (2) enable nested group expansion on sync, (3) add a fast-path invalidate webhook from idp when lifecycle_event occurs. my preference: 3 + 2. webhook (3) ensures immediate invalidation, expansion (2) fixes membership fidelity.
samir: we already have a webhook consumer but it's rate-limited. increasing priority for lifecycle events is doable. I'll open a short PR to: a) add `lifecycle_priority` topic to the queue, b) add hashed-email flag in log schema.
maya: can you ping me in the PR? i'd like a quick code review. also we'll need a short security review on storing raw email in audit index — @sophia can you own the ticket to Legal?
sophia: yes, I'll file the ticket and loop Legal + Compliance. estimated 1 day for approval.
maya: cool. action items I have: reduce cache for sensitive routes (config patch), coordinate webhook priority change, update log producer to hash emails. samir to PR, jonathan to add invalidation path in auth runtime, sophia to handle Legal.
jonathan: I'll add a small endpoint `/auth/invalidate/:user_id` that consumes idp webhooks and nukes KV entries for that user. will make it idempotent.
samir: PR opened: https://git.redwood/internal/pulls/4821 — tagging @maya for review. :eyes:
maya: looking now. if all good i'll merge and roll to canary tonight.
infra-bot: deploy bot — canary deploy queued for `auth-service` (v2.14.3-canary) — triggered by samir at 1769991240.
maya: thanks everyone. small ask: please avoid putting full emails into ephemeral debug outputs (sentry) until Legal signs off. :no_entry_sign:
jonathan: noted. I'll add a Sentry scrubber rule for `user.email` tonight.
maya: resolving here — will post outcome and the Legal ticket link when available. :white_check_mark:
